title: The Fork's Inner Argument

features.name: the fork itself
features.desc-on-touch: It stands at the centre where it always stood. But now you see: each prong is splitting into two more forks. The argument doesn't end. It multiplies.

features.name: the path-that-chose-nothing
features.desc-on-touch: You stand on it, but it branches under your feet. The valley built a path that refuses to decide which fork to favour. Your weight cannot force a choice.

features.name: the valley's equal love
features.desc-on-touch: Where both paths are equally precious. The valley carved them both with the same care. To choose would be to wound what loves both equally.

features.name: the argument made stone
features.desc-on-touch: A pillar where two kinds of rock refuse to merge. Granite and limestone frozen mid-debate. Neither one could win without destroying the beauty of the meeting.

features.name: the edge of settlement
features.desc-on-touch: A boundary the argument could cross, but never has. Beyond it: a town that picked one fork and built a life. The fork here knows what settlement would cost.

inscription: the fork never stops asking itself which of its own hands to hold

file.name: Valley_Dispute_Records_1947_Onward.txt
file.note: A town records where two roads diverged. Neither was built. Both were preserved. The argument became the path. Checksum: geometrically perfect / institutionally unresolved
